title: Core vs Non-Core Vaccine Planning
content: Vaccination plans should be individualized for each dog. Core vaccines are broadly recommended, while non-core vaccines should be selected based on lifestyle, geography, and exposure risk in discussion with a veterinarian.

title: Leptospirosis Included in Core Protection
content: AAHA's updated guidance includes leptospirosis in core recommendations for dogs, highlighting both canine health and zoonotic risk considerations when planning preventive care.

title: Global Vaccination Framework for Dogs
content: WSAVA guidelines support evidence-based vaccination with attention to regional disease pressure, patient age, and risk profile instead of one-size-fits-all schedules.

title: Nutrition Assessment as a Clinical Vital Sign
content: Nutrition should be routinely assessed using body condition, muscle condition, life stage, and clinical status. Feeding plans should be adjusted gradually and monitored over time.

title: How to Evaluate Dog Food Quality Claims
content: Ingredient lists alone do not determine quality. Owners should use broader nutritional and manufacturer-quality indicators and review diets with their veterinarian.

title: Humane Dog Training Methods
content: AVSAB recommends reward-based methods for training and behavior modification. Aversive tools and punishment-based methods are associated with welfare and relationship risks.

title: Puppy Socialization Position Guidance
content: Early, structured socialization can reduce later fear and behavior problems. Socialization plans should be safe, positive, and coordinated with veterinary preventive care.

title: Dog Bite and Scratch Prevention
content: Most dog bites are preventable. Supervision, safe handling around dogs, and avoiding interactions when dogs are stressed, sleeping, eating, or guarding resources reduce risk.

title: Pet Food Safety and Infection Risk
content: Pet food and treats can carry germs. Safe handling and hygiene are important for both pet and family health, and diet choices should be discussed with a veterinarian.

title: Tick Prevention for Dogs
content: Daily tick checks and veterinarian-guided prevention products are important for reducing tickborne disease risk in dogs and for limiting ticks entering the home.

title: Heartworm Disease Basics and Prevention
content: Heartworm disease can be severe and is mosquito-borne. Prevention and routine testing are key, and treatment is more complex and risky than prevention.

title: American Heartworm Society Guidance
content: AHS guidelines support year-round prevention, routine testing, and evidence-based diagnosis and treatment workflows under veterinary supervision.

title: FDA-Approved Preventive Use Overview
content: Consistent preventive use and adherence to veterinary recommendations are central to heartworm control. Missed doses increase infection risk.

title: Immediate Steps for Suspected Poisoning
content: If poisoning is suspected, immediate veterinary or poison-control consultation is advised. Delays and unsupervised home remedies can worsen outcomes.

title: Household Food Hazards for Dogs
content: Some common foods can cause severe toxicity in dogs. Rapid assessment and timely veterinary treatment are critical after known or suspected ingestion.

title: Canine Life Stage Wellness Structure
content: Preventive care should be matched to life stage, with regular rechecks and proactive counseling for behavior, nutrition, and disease prevention.

title: Practical Vaccine Table Use in Decision Support
content: WSAVA vaccination tables can support consistent risk-based decisions, including core vaccine timing and non-core recommendations based on exposure profile.

title: Routine Vet Checkups and Preventive Parasite Control
content: Regular veterinary checkups, vaccination review, and parasite prevention are key parts of keeping dogs healthy and reducing zoonotic and household risk.

title: Year-Round Heartworm Prevention Emphasis
content: Year-round heartworm prevention is recommended because mosquitoes and exposure risk can persist beyond peak seasons, and prevention is safer than treatment.

title: Canine Parvovirus Basics
content: Canine parvovirus can cause severe gastrointestinal illness, especially in unvaccinated puppies. Early veterinary assessment and preventive vaccination are central to reducing serious outcomes.

title: Managing Separation-Related Anxiety in Dogs
content: Separation-related distress is a behavioral welfare issue that should be managed with gradual desensitization, predictable routines, and professional behavioral support where needed.

title: Puppy Feeding Fundamentals
content: Puppies require complete and balanced growth-stage nutrition with feeding amounts adjusted for age, size, and body condition. Diet transitions should be gradual and monitored.

title: Welfare Risks of Pronged Collars
content: Aversive training tools can negatively affect welfare and behavior outcomes. Humane, reward-based approaches are preferred for long-term behavior change and safety.

title: Routine Healthcare for Dogs
content: Routine canine healthcare includes vaccination planning, parasite control, dental and general health monitoring, and regular veterinary checks based on life stage and risk.

title: Heat Safety for Dogs
content: Dogs can develop life-threatening heat illness quickly in warm conditions. Owners should provide shade, cool water, and avoid high-heat exercise, with urgent vet care for heat stress signs.

title: Preparing Pets for Hot Weather Emergencies
content: Emergency planning for pets during heat and disaster conditions includes transport readiness, access to water and shelter, and early action before severe weather peaks.

title: Leptospirosis in Pets
content: Leptospirosis can affect dogs and people. Risk reduction includes environmental precautions, early veterinary assessment when symptoms appear, and prevention planning with a veterinarian.

title: Pain Management Guidelines
content: Pain assessment should be integrated into routine veterinary care. Timely recognition and multimodal management improve welfare and recovery outcomes in dogs.

title: WHO Position on Rabies Control Through Dog Vaccination
content: WHO guidance emphasizes vaccination of dogs as a core strategy for preventing dog-mediated rabies and protecting communities in at-risk regions.
